_roadWidth: MEASURED off the painted lane, not assumed: the median clearance from the cyan centre stroke to the nearest pixel that is not road, doubled. Narrowest 22.2 and widest 46.2 canvas px on the half-width; the median is the honest number because the lane has to fit its narrowest stretch. Level 1's road is 80.0, so this one is 18% tighter and every lateral figure derived from it moves with it.
note: EVERY NUMBER HERE IS DERIVED FROM tools/level2_path_overlay.png, which is the volcanic plate with the lane's centre stroked in cyan and fifteen tower pads ringed and numbered in green. That is the difference from level 1: this plate came with its route drawn on it, so nothing here is a classifier's guess about what is road. Re-derive with `python3 tools/check_level2.py --emit` after any re-export, and check the stored file against the art with `python3 tools/check_level2.py`. The overlay lives under tools/ and NOT under public/, because everything in public/ is deployed whether or not anything references it and this is 1.9MB that only that one script opens. VERIFY THE OVERLAY BEFORE DERIVING FROM IT: the correct file has 9641 pixels matching R<60 G>200 B>200. A superseded export went round with its cyan stroke one pixel thinner (7623), and because roadWidth is a median of integer distances measured along that stroke, deriving from it silently moved roadWidth 65.8 -> 67.6 and the waypoint count 49 -> 47 while the painted route had not moved at all.
_waypoints: Douglas-Peucker at 1.1 overlay px over the traced centre of the cyan stroke. MEASURED, not asserted: check_level2.py walks the painted centreline and reports the worst distance from it to this polyline, and that number is 1.0 OVERLAY px (0.9 canvas px) against a stroke four px wide, so the route is inside the paint for its whole length. The note used to claim 0.6, which was a number from an earlier epsilon that nothing re-measured after the epsilon moved — a file documenting a figure its own check disagreed with. THE TWO END POINTS ARE EXTENSIONS, NOT TRACED: enemies walk in from off the plate at x=-60 and out at x=1340, and each of those is a new point on the line the lane is already travelling when it reaches the edge. Level 1 drags its end waypoints out to those x values in place, which is free on that plate because its lane meets both edges flat. This lane arrives on a slope, and the same drag swung the opening segment 13 overlay px off the paint.
_buildSpots: FIFTEEN RINGS, FIFTEEN PADS, one to one. The overlay used to ring seventeen candidates for fifteen pads, and check_level2.py printed the two leftovers on every run because a script cannot know whether a spot was dropped on purpose. The re-drawn overlay rings exactly what it means, so that warning is gone and an unmatched ring is now a real disagreement. Order is the overlay's reading order, top to bottom, and carries no meaning. SPACING IS NOW THE GAME'S, NOT THE PAINTER'S. A node's tap radius is spotRadius, so two pads need 2 x spotRadius = 68 px between centres before their tap targets stop overlapping. The previous ring set was packed at a 59.0 px minimum — pads 2-5 at 59.0 and 5-7 at 59.6 were two pairs of overlapping tap targets, which is one mis-tap each. This set is packed at 72.1 (its closest pair, 4-6), clearing 68 by 4.1. tests/level2.test.ts asserts that floor so a future overlay cannot quietly reintroduce the overlap. THE TAP RADIUS IS NOT THE ADJUSTABLE END OF THIS. Dropping spotRadius to 28 would also separate tight pads, and it is the wrong fix: world 1280 renders to 844 CSS px, so 34 world px is a 44.8 px tap diameter and 28 is 36.9, under the 44 pt minimum a thumb needs. The pads move, not the radius. FIVE PADS SIT ON PAINTED ROCK — 2 (1050.7, 216.0), 7 (884.4, 451.6), 10 (944.9, 547.6), 12 (772.4, 606.2) and 13 (510.2, 612.4) — rather than on open ground. THAT IS DELIBERATE AND ACCEPTED, NOT AN OVERSIGHT TO FIX. The plate's right third has no clean flat ground beside the lane, and leaving those stretches of the route uncovered by any buildable spot is worse than standing a pad on rock. Do not 'correct' these five back onto grass; there is none there to move them to.
_heroStart: MEASURED AGAINST THE PAINTED PLATE WITH THE SPRITE'S REAL HEIGHT, not derived from clearances alone. He is about 120 world px tall, and the value this replaces — (588.0, 128.0) — put his feet at y=128, which is above the lane's own highest point of 163.7: his head was over the top edge of the board and his footprint was in a lava field, 129 px of it. This position was chosen by requiring his whole 120x55 footprint to be clear of molten rock and then keeping the clearances that made the old spot look reasonable. What it measures: 0 lava pixels under him and 109.3 px to the nearest lava, 94.2 px from the road's edge, and 84.5 px from the nearest pad (that last figure moved with the re-drawn pad rings; it was 78.9 against the previous set). Re-check with `python3 tools/check_level2.py`.
